skills_considered.reason: The reading pipeline itself: M0 packet, acquisition, section-by-section read, manifest, receipt.

Not opened in full: the packet's acquisition procedure was OPEN but the first proof-of-work route won the complete article on the first attempt and a second independent route corroborated it byte-identically, so the tiered cascade had nothing left to resolve.

None of its four triggers fired: this reading contradicts no persisted locator (no prior manifest exists for this PMID) and it narrows, reverses, corroborates or removes no consolidated baseline claim - the dossier proposes, and any claim-level movement is routed with an R4 precondition rather than taken here.
The transferable leads are already captured as locators and as queue entry FT-178; a discovery pass would restate them without adding a lead this manifest does not carry.
This paper matures no therapeutic lever toward the reference genotype: the tissue is lung, the endpoint is vascular leak, and its one positive inflammatory result is ex vivo in isolated cells.
No candidate molecule and no SMILES anywhere in this reading; SP600125 appears only as a research-tool JNK inhibitor that failed to rescue.
Refused on principle for this task: it needs an API key and external traffic, and external spend of any kind is a reserved act under LEGEND_CORE 21d that is never mine.

group_assessment.weighting: Two different groups sit on this paper and they must be weighted differently. The SENIOR group is Singla's pulmonary/critical-care laboratory at Illinois: 19 publications under 'Singla Sunit'[Full Author Name] and 4 of them on WWOX (measured 2026-09-13) - primary for ARDS and lung endothelial barrier biology, a recent entrant on this gene. The bare 'Singla S'[au] count is 794 and is NOT one person; it is not used. Aldaz, 8th of 13, is primary for the GENE - 66 publications under 'Aldaz C Marcelo'[Full Author Name], 28 on WWOX - and his contribution here is stated in the Methods as a REAGENT, the WWOXflox/flox mouse of reference 24, not as data or analysis (Author Contributions place him under conception/design and manuscript preparation, not data acquisition). NEITHER group is primary for the disease this repository models: nobody on this paper works on WWOX-related neurodevelopmental disease and the word brain does not occur in the article. The consequence cuts in the paper's favour on exactly the part that matters most here: the central result is a NEGATIVE about inflammation produced by the laboratory whose own prior paper (reference 20) reported the positive, so the observation is made against the group's own prior interest and is strengthened by that, while the interpretation - an 'inflammation-independent' mechanism - is the group's hypothesis and is weighted as a hypothesis and not as a result.

field_density.reading: The intersection this paper occupies is nearly empty and the contrast is the point: 6 records for WWOX and lung injury/ARDS and 14 for WWOX and endothelium, against 136 for WWOX and brain/neurodevelopment/epilepsy, out of 708 WWOX records. In a rare disease a near-empty intersection is a signal and not an absence - but it also means this leg of the axis rests on a handful of papers from one laboratory, and the 2 records for WWOX and e-cigarettes are this paper and its own preprint.

queued.why: Reference 20 is this paper's own antecedent and the only source in this corpus for a POSITIVE inflammatory phenotype from lung WWOX loss. This paper cites it five times and every time by contrast. It is CORPUS-STUB-091, identity only, never opened. Reading it is the precondition for saying whether the whole-lung and endothelial models measure the same phenomenon.

multihop.not_queued_and_why: Two gene-direct references resolve to no record on any registry surface - PMID 29384700 (the e-cigarette exposure model this paper uses) and PMID 25517572 (WWOX CNV and COPD). They are named in FT-178's body rather than given entries of their own because no conclusion I draw rests on either; they are corpus gaps, not premises. Of the remaining six, five are identity-only CORPUS records and one, PMID 19936220 (reference 24, the floxed allele), is already read here with receipt FTR-20260806-19936220-01.

retraction_check.result: NO retraction, erratum or expression of concern on this PMID, and the two notice routes DISAGREED about what notices exist, so both are recorded. Europe PMC resultType=core commentCorrectionList (2026-09-13) returns exactly two items: 'Comment in' -> PMID 33105088 (an editorial in the same issue, Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol 2021;64(1):10-11, doi 10.1165/rcmb.2020-0444ED) and 'Preprint in' -> PPR187117 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2020.07.13.200832). NCBI ESummary for the same PMID returns an EMPTY commentscorrections field in JSON and no CommentsCorrections block at all in XML, so an ESummary-only check would have reported no notices whatever. A 'Comment in' is a comment and not a correction, and the editorial is not part of this lot. erratum_scope_check.py, re-run once this manifest existed, reports all erratum mentions negated, 1 manifest examined, CLEAN 1 - and its own verdict line says it judges nothing. The article prints no retraction or correction notice on any of its 11 pages.

dependencies.citing_relation: No dependency was flagged, so there is no citing_relation to state. 61 of 66 references carried a DOI and were screened against the 2026-09-10 integrity snapshot with zero hits; the 5 UNSCREENABLE_NO_DOI are older pre-DOI citations and their integrity status is unknown rather than clean.

retraction_check.corrected_items_why: EMPTY BY FACT, NOT UNDECLARED. There is no erratum, correction, corrigendum or expression of concern on this article, so the set of corrected panels is empty and no locator in this manifest can stand on one. The words 'erratum' and 'correction' appear in this block only inside the statement that none exists and in the names of the tools that were run. Recorded because erratum_scope_check.py selects deliberately widely on those words and then, finding no structured scope, returns SCOPE_UNDECLARED = INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than assuming clean - which is the correct refusal. I first hypothesised that the OPEN state was a token artefact of the tool's own verdict sentence; the --json run refuted that (status SCOPE_UNDECLARED, CLEAN 0, INSUFFICIENT_DATA 1), so the hypothesis is withdrawn here rather than left standing, and the scope is declared instead of argued about.

preprint_comparison.finding: Checked once, as the contract requires. The two headline quantities are IDENTICAL between preprint abstract and published paper: 47% decrease in WWOX mRNA in current versus former/never smokers, and an average 57% decrease after nicotine-containing e-cigarette vapour. The author list differs by one - Shakir Z appears in the published paper and not in the preprint record - and the title expands 'ARDS' to 'Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome'. LIMIT DECLARED: this is an abstract-level and metadata-level comparison of the preprint RECORD, not a line-by-line comparison of the preprint full text, which was not retrieved. No difference bearing on any conclusion I draw was found, and I cannot exclude one in sections I did not compare.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: Europe PMC inEPMC=Y, inPMC=Y and fullTextIdList=[PMC7780991], measured 2026-09-13 on both resultType=core and resultType=idlist. So the article IS full-text indexed and these quotes are externally locatable by a third party through the PMC reader. THE QUALIFICATION THAT MATTERS: isOpenAccess=N and the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returns HTTP 404 with 0 bytes, while NCBI efetch db=pmc returns front matter plus an explicit publisher refusal of the full text in XML form. Indexed is therefore NOT the same as machine-retrievable here: an external verifier can read the sentences on the PMC page or in the PDF but cannot fetch a structured surface to match them against, which is exactly why every text locator in this manifest is adjudicated on a page crop.
